cohort: The study included 600 full-term neonates of both sexes, with birth weight > 2.5 kg, who were within the neonatal period and attended a dermatology outpatient department in Andhra Pradesh, India.
finding: A high prevalence (87.3%) of dermatoses was found in neonates, with Mongolian Spots, Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum, and Physiological Desquamation being most common, and dermatoses were associated with high parity, vaginal delivery, and consanguinity.
mod_finding: Naevi and Physiological Desquamation were associated with vaginal deliveries.
